Coast Basketball League|WCBL]] All-Rookie First Team (2009) }} '''Jonathan Mychal Gibson''' (born November 8, 1987){{cite web|url=http://www.scoresway.com/zgorzelec?sport=basketball&page=player&id=5671|title=JONATHAN MYCHAL GIBSON | POINT GUARD|work=Scoresway.com|access-date=April 12, 2017}} is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Al-Ula (basketball)|Al-Ula]] of the [[Saudi Basketball League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for [[New Mexico State Aggies men's basketball|New Mexico State]] before playing professionally in Turkey, Israel, Italy, China and Iran. He made a name for himself in China, earning the league's [[List of Chinese Basketball Association scoring leaders|scoring title]] in both the 2013–14 and the 2015–16 season, with 32.5 and 42 points per game respectively. ==High school career== Gibson attended Calvary Christian Prep School in [[San Fernando, California]]. As a senior in 2005–06, he averaged 23.3 points, 5.2 rebounds, 7.1 assists and 3.1 steals per game, as he led Calvary Christian to a 22–3 record and was named the most valuable player of the San Antonio League and a first team all-conference selection.{{cite web|url=http://www.nmstatesports.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=1635|title=New Mexico State Athletics – Jonathan Gibson – 2009–10|work=NMStateSports.com|access-date=July 16, 2016}} On May 2, 2006, Gibson signed a [[National Letter of Intent]] to play [[college basketball]] for [[New Mexico State University]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/espn/wire?section=ncb&id=2430882|title=California prep star Gibson signs with Aggies|work=ESPN.com|date=May 2, 2006|access-date=July 16, 2016}} ==College career== As a freshman at [[New Mexico State Aggies men's basketball|New Mexico State]] in 2006–07, Gibson averaged 2.6 points in 31 games, and finished with 22 assists. He twice had a 12-point performance during the season. In the WAC Tournament title game against [[Utah State Aggies men's basketball|Utah State]] on March 10, 2007, Gibson scored two late points on a reverse lay-up to help NMSU secure their first [[Western Athletic Conference|WAC]] title. In his first [[2007 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|NCAA Tournament]] appearance, Gibson scored two points on 2-for-2 shooting from the free-throw line in nine minutes. As a sophomore in 2007–08, Gibson appeared in all 35 games, earning 32 starting assignments, and averaged 12.2 points per game, which was second on the team. Gibson was a scoring threat as he shot 45.4% from the field, 41.9% from three-point range, and 75.6% from the free-throw line. He scored in double-figures in 24 games and reached the 20-point or more plateau on five occasions. He also had 55 assists and 33 steals. On February 9, 2008, he scored a career-high 24 points against [[Boise State Broncos men's basketball|Boise State]]. The Aggies ended the season winning 10 of the final 12 games and Gibson was in double-figures in nine of those contests. In the triple overtime thriller against Boise State on March 15 in the WAC title game, Gibson played a career-high 51 minutes and contributed 15 points. As a junior in 2008–09, Gibson averaged 14.1 points per game, which ranked second on the team and 10th in the WAC. As a 30-game starter, Gibson surpassed the 20-point plateau five times. He posted a .426 field goal percentage and a .387 three-point field goal percentage, and ranked third on the squad in assists with 65 and tied for first on the squad with 44 steals. He led the Aggies in scoring in three games with a season-best 22 points against [[New Mexico Lobos men's basketball|New Mexico]] on December 30, 2008, and in both games of the WAC Tournament, with 22 points against Boise State on March 12 and 16 against Utah State on March 13. As a senior in 2009–10, Gibson averaged 17.5 points, 2.9 rebounds, 2.8 assists and 1.4 steals in 34 games while shooting 44.7% (197–441 FGs) from the field, 40.6% (106–261 3FGs) from three-point range and 84.8% (95–112 FTs) from the free throw line. He was named All-WAC Second Team and led the WAC in three-pointers made, ranked second in 3FG%, fifth in scoring average, fourth in FT%, eighth in FG% and seventh in steals per game.{{cite web|first=Arya|last=Ahmadi|url=https://www.mavs.com/mavericks-sign-guard-jonathan-gibson/|title=Mavericks sign guard Jonathan Gibson|work=Mavs.com|date=July 15, 2016|access-date=July 16, 2016}} Gibson finished with 1,541 career points at NMSU, which is seventh in program history, and was part of two Western Athletic Conference Tournament championship teams in 2007 and 2010.{{cite web|first=Mark|last=Rudi|url=https://www.lcsun-news.com/story/sports/college/blogs/off-the-mark/2016/03/28/johnathan-gibson-1st-nmsu-alum-announced-nmsu-unm-alumni-game/82360880/|title=Jonathan Gibson .398 || .758 || 1.9 || 1.8 || 1.0 || .0 || 11.8 |- {{S-end}} ==Professional career== ===2010–11 season=== On July 21, 2010, Gibson signed a one-year deal with [[Oyak Renault]] of the [[Turkish Basketball Super League]].{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/83393/oyak-renault-tabs-rookie-jonathan-gibson.html|title=Oyak Renault tabs rookie Jonathan Gibson|work=Sportando.com|date=July 21, 2010|access-date=July 16, 2016}} On December 27, 2010, he parted ways with Oyak. In 11 games for the club, he averaged 18.1 points, 3.9 rebounds, 3.3 assists and 2.0 steals per game.{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/84569/jonathan-gibson-and-oyak-renault-part-ways.html|title=Jonathan Gibson and Oyak Renault part ways|work=Sportando.com|date=December 27, 2010|access-date=July 16, 2016}} On January 12, 2011, he signed with [[Ironi Ashkelon]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]] for the rest of the season.{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/israel/84908/jonathan-gibson-inks-with-ironi-ashkelon.html|title=Jonathan Gibson inks with Ironi Ashkelon|work=Sportando.com|date=January 12, 2011|access-date=July 16, 2016}} In 16 games for Ironi, he averaged 7.3 points, 1.1 rebounds and 1.3 assists per game. ===2011–12 season=== On September 28, 2011, Gibson signed a one-year deal with [[Trabzonspor B.K.|Trabzonspor]] of the [[Turkish Basketball Super League]].{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/88522/jonathan-gibson-inks-with-trabzonspor.html|title=Jonathan Gibson inks with Trabzonspor|work=Sportando.com|date=September 28, 2011|access-date=July 16, 2016}} Despite a poor season for Trabzonspor, [[2011–12 Turkish Basketball League|a campaign]] that saw them go 6–24, Gibson averaged a league-best 19.9 points per game. He left the team prior to their season finale, and in 29 games, he also averaged 2.5 rebounds and 3.7 assists per game.{{cite web|url=http://basketball.eurobasket.com/team/Turkey/Trabzonspor_Medical_Park_Basketbol/191?Page=3&Stats=2012|title=Trabzonspor Medical Park Basketbol basketball team – 2011–12 stats|work=Eurobasket.com|access-date=July 16, 2016}} On April 24, 2012, Gibson signed with [[New Basket Brindisi|Enel Brindisi]] of the [[Serie A2 Basket|Legadue]] for the rest of the season.{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a2-est/91542/enel-brindisi-announces-jonathan-gibson.html|title=Enel Brindisi announces Jonathan Gibson|work=Sportando.com|date=April 24, 2012|access-date=July 16, 2016}} He made his debut for Brindisi on May 5, in the team's regular season finale. They finished the regular season in third place on the ladder with an 18–10 record. Brindisi breezed through the quarter-finals and semi-finals, winning both series 3–0. In the Finals, they defeated [[Pistoia Basket 2000|Giorgo Tesi PT]] 3–1 to win the league's playoff championship.{{cite web|url=http://www.eurobasket.com/Italy/basketball-League-A2_2011-2012.asp|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160822180423/http://www.eurobasket.com/Italy/basketball-League-A2_2011-2012.asp|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 22, 2016|title=Italy Serie A2 Season 2011–2012|work=Eurobasket.com|access-date=July 16, 2016}} Gibson dominated throughout the playoffs, and over 11 games for Brindisi (10 playoff, one regular season), he averaged 24.1 points, 3.5 rebounds, 3.4 assists and 1.5 steals per game. Winning the Legadue playoffs led to Brindisi being promoted to the [[Lega Basket Serie A]] for the 2012–13 season.{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/92656/virtus-bologna-eyeing-jonathan-gibson.html|title=Virtus Bologna eyeing Jonathan Gibson|work=Sportando.com|date=June 22, 2012|access-date=July 16, 2016}} ===2012–13 season=== In July 2012, Gibson joined the [[Boston Celtics]] for the [[2012 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/usa/nba/92962/jonathan-gibson-will-play-nba-summer-league-with-celtics.html|title=Jonathan Gibson will play NBA Summer League with Celtics|work=Sportando.com|date=July 1, 2012|access-date=July 16, 2016}} The Celtics went 4–1 at the Orlando Summer League and 2–3 at the Las Vegas Summer League. In 10 games for the Celtics, Gibson averaged 7.0 points, 1.3 rebounds and 1.6 assists in 12.8 minutes per game.{{cite web|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/nba/teams/Boston-Celtics/2/Rosters/Summer_League/2012|title=2012 Boston Celtics NBA Summer League Roster|work=RealGM.com|access-date=July 16, 2016}} On July 7, 2012, Gibson re-signed with [[New Basket Brindisi|Enel Brindisi]] on a one-year deal.{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/93223/enel-brindisi-keeps-jonathan-gibson-with-an-nba-out.html|title=Enel Brindisi keeps Jonathan Gibson with an NBA out|work=Sportando.com|date=July 7, 2012|access-date=July 16, 2016}} Brindisi finished the [[2012–13 Lega Basket Serie A|2012–13 season]] in 12th place on the ladder with an 11–19 record, missing the playoffs in their first season back in the top league. Gibson appeared in all 30 games during the season, averaging 18.4 points (second in the league),{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/101071/serie-a-regular-season-statistical-leaders.html|title=Serie A Regular Season statistical leaders|work=Sportando.com|date=May 6, 2013|access-date=July 16, 2016}} 2.7 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 1.4 steals per game. ===2013–14 season=== In August 2013, Gibson signed a one-year deal with the [[Zhejiang Lions]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]].{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/104484/jonathan-gibson-moving-to-guangsha-in-cba.html|title=Jonathan Gibson moving to Guangsha in CBA|work=Sportando.com|date=August 1, 2013|access-date=July 16, 2016}}{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/104600/zhejiang-guangsha-lions-officially-announced-jonathan-gibson.html|title=Zhejiang Guangsha Lions officially announced Jonathan Gibson|work=Sportando.com|date=August 5, 2013|access-date=July 16, 2016}} Gibson had a monster year with Zhejiang, appearing in 33 of 34 regular season games, missing only a January 10 game against the [[Beijing Ducks]].{{cite web|url=http://www.eurobasket.com/boxScores/China/2014/0110_941_7304.asp|title=Regular Season Round 23: Beijing Ducks – Guangsha L. 114–104|work=Eurobasket.com|date=January 10, 2014|access-date=July 16, 2016}} During the regular season, he scored 40 points or more four times, including a 46-point effort on January 8 against [[Tianjin Ronggang|Tianjin]]. Zhejiang finished the regular season in fifth place on the ladder with a 21–13 record. Gibson won the league's [[List of Chinese Basketball Association scoring leaders|scoring title]] with a 31.7-points-per-game average. In Game 1 of their quarter-final match-up with Beijing, Gibson scored 54 points{{cite web|first=David|last=Pick|url=https://twitter.com/iamdpick/status/436160369187627008|title=Jonathan Gibson, China's top scorer, went...|work=Twitter|date=February 19, 2014|access-date=July 16, 2016}} to help Zhejiang win the game 113–110. However, the Lions went on to lose the next three games to bow out of the playoffs with a 3–1 defeat.{{cite web|url=http://www.asia-basket.com/China/basketball-League-CBA_2013-2014.asp|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140423000807/http://www.asia-basket.com/China/basketball-League-CBA_2013-2014.asp|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 23, 2014|title=China CBA Season 2013–2014|work=Eurobasket.com|access-date=July 16, 2016}} Gibson averaged 39 points per game over the four quarter-final games.{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/112123/americans-in-cba-quarterfinals-stats.html|title=Americans in CBA: Quarterfinals' stats|work=Sportando.com|date=February 26, 2014|access-date=July 16, 2016}} Following the conclusion of the [[2013–14 CBA season]], Gibson was offered a guaranteed deal by Russian club [[BC Nizhny Novgorod|Nizhny Novgorod]],{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/russia/112635/nizhny-novgorod-offers-a-guaranteed-deal-to-jonathan-gibson.html|title=Nizhny Novgorod offers a guaranteed deal to Jonathan Gibson|work=Sportando.com|date=March 3, 2014|access-date=July 16, 2016}} but he turned it down.{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/russia/112996/jonathan-gibson-turns-down-offer-from-nizhny-novgorod.html|title=Jonathan Gibson turns down offer from Nizhny Novgorod|work=Sportando.com|date=March 6, 2014|access-date=July 16, 2016}} He later signed a one-month deal with Iranian club [[Petrochimi Bandar Imam BC|Petrochimi Imam]] on April 1, 2014.{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/115744/jonathan-gibson-signs-a-one-month-deal-with-petrochimi.html|title=Jonathan Gibson signs a one-month deal with Petrochimi|work=Sportando.com|date=April 1, 2014|access-date=July 16, 2016}} He made his debut for Petrochimi on April 20 in Game 1 of the team's semi-final series against [[Zob Ahan Isfahan BC|Zob Ahan]]. Petrochimi went on to sweep the series in three games to move onto the Finals. There they defeated [[Mahram Tehran BC|Mahram Tehran]] 4–1 to win their second straight title. Gibson scored 41 points in a Game 5 victory.{{cite web|url=https://theiranproject.com/blog/2014/05/10/petrochimi-retains-iran-basketball-super-league-title/|title=Petrochimi retains Iran Basketball Super League title|work=TheIranProject.com|date=May 10, 2014|access-date=July 16, 2016}} In eight games for Petrochimi, Gibson averaged 30.9 points, 4.5 rebounds, 2.6 assists and 1.8 steals per game. ===2014–15 season=== In July 2014, Gibson joined the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] for the [[2014 NBA Summer League]],{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-summer-league-roster/|title=TRAIL BLAZERS ANNOUNCE 2014 SAMSUNG NBA SUMMER LEAGUE ROSTER|work=NBA.com|date=July 7, 2014|access-date=July 16, 2016}} but he managed just one game and played a total of six minutes.{{cite web|first=Bobby|last=Karalla|url=http://www.mavs.com/no-glitz-no-glamour-jonathan-gibsons-rise-summer-league-sensation/|title=No glitz, no glamour: Jonathan Gibson's rise to Summer League sensation|work=Mavs.com|date=July 14, 2016|access-date=July 16, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170218014824/https://www.mavs.com/no-glitz-no-glamour-jonathan-gibsons-rise-summer-league-sensation/|archive-date=February 18, 2017|url-status=dead}} Following his time with the Trail Blazers, Gibson signed a two-year deal with the [[Zhejiang Lions]], returning to the club for a second stint.{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/167222/jonathan-gibson-leaving-zhejiang-guangsha-to-sign-with-tianjin-steel.html|title=Jonathan Gibson leaving Zhejiang Guangsha to sign with TianJin Steel?|work=Sportando.com|date=July 5, 2015|access-date=July 16, 2016}} However, in early October, he suffered a foot injury and was ruled out for four to six weeks.{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/136927/jonathan-gibson-will-miss-from-4-to-6-weeks-of-action.html|title=Jonathan Gibson will miss from 4-to-6 weeks of action|work=Sportando.com|date=October 7, 2014|access-date=July 16, 2016}}{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/137008/zhejiang-guangsha-sign-jamaal-franklin-to-replace-jonathan-gibson.html|title=Zhejiang Guangsha sign Jamaal Franklin to replace Jonathan Gibson|work=Sportando.com|date=October 8, 2014|access-date=July 16, 2016}} On January 7, 2015, he was ruled out for the entire [[2014–15 CBA season]] in order to rehab his broken foot.{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/147722/guangsha-s-jonathan-gibson-out-for-china-season-with-broken-foot.html|title=Guangsha's Jonathan Gibson out for China season with broken foot|work=Sportando.com|date=January 7, 2015|access-date=July 16, 2016}} On March 17, 2015, Gibson signed with [[Petrochimi Bandar Imam BC|Petrochimi Imam]] for the 2015 [[WABA Champions Cup]],{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/155629/jonathan-gibson-signs-with-petrochimi.html|title=Jonathan Gibson signs with Petrochimi|work=Sportando.com|date=March 17, 2015|access-date=July 16, 2016}} but the competition never went ahead. ===2015–16 season=== In July 2015, Gibson parted ways with Zhejiang after terminating his contract with the team.{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/173360/qingdao-double-star-nearing-to-a-deal-with-jonathan-gibson.html|title=Qingdao Double Star nearing to a deal with Jonathan Gibson|work=Sportando.com|date=August 20, 2015|access-date=July 16, 2016}} On August 30, 2015, he signed a one-year deal with fellow Chinese team [[Qingdao DoubleStar]].{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/174363/qingdao-eagles-sign-jonathan-gibson.html|title=Qingdao Eagles sign Jonathan Gibson|work=Sportando.com|date=August 30, 2015|access-date=July 16, 2016}} Gibson bested his 2013–14 CBA campaign by scoring 40 points or more in 24 games, including 50 points or more in four games. On December 13, 2015, he scored a career-high 56 points in a 138–124 win over [[Jiangsu Monkey King|Jiangsu Tongxi]].{{cite web|url=http://m.chinadaily.com.cn/cn/2015-12/13/content_22704060.htm|title=CBA roundup: Defending champions Beijing enjoy three straight wins|work=ChinaDaily.com.cn|date=December 13, 2015|access-date=July 16, 2016|archive-date=August 19, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160819133734/http://m.chinadaily.com.cn/cn/2015-12/13/content_22704060.htm|url-status=dead}} Despite his dominant individual season, Qingdao missed the playoffs with a 16–22 record. He averaged 42.0 points per game on the season, thus winning the CBA scoring title for the second time in three years. He appeared in 36 of the team's 38 games in 2015–16, and also averaged 6.7 rebounds, 5.1 assists and 2.1 steals per game. ===2016–17 season=== In July 2016, Gibson joined the [[Dallas Mavericks]] for the [[2016 NBA Summer League|2016 Las Vegas Summer League]]. At 28 years old, he was one of the oldest players in Vegas. He quickly became a Summer League sensation after scoring 30 points in his debut on July 9 against the [[Miami Heat]].{{cite web|first=Mark|last=Rudi|url=https://www.lcsun-news.com/story/sports/college/blogs/off-the-mark/2016/07/10/former-nmsu-guard-gibson-scores-30-mavericks-summer-league/86914348/|title=Former NMSU guard Gibson scores 30 points for Mavericks in Summer League|work=LCSun-News.com|date=July 9, 2016|access-date=July 16, 2016}} Three days later, he had a 26-point outing against the [[Boston Celtics]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160712/BOSDAL/gameinfo.html|title=Recap: Celtics 88, Mavericks 82|work=NBA.com|date=July 12, 2016|access-date=July 16, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170217044518/http://www.nba.com/games/20160712/BOSDAL/gameinfo.html|archive-date=February 17, 2017|url-status=dead}} His impressive Summer League display led to a contract offer from Mavericks, and on July 15, Gibson signed a partially guaranteed three-year deal with the team.{{cite web|url=http://www.kvia.com/sports/Former-NMSU-star-Jonathan-Gibson-signed-by-Dallas-Mavericks/40701084|title=Former NMSU star Jonathan Gibson signed by Dallas Mavericks|work=KVIA.com|date=July 13, 2016|access-date=July 16, 2016|archive-date=August 26, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160826004243/http://www.kvia.com/sports/Former-NMSU-star-Jonathan-Gibson-signed-by-Dallas-Mavericks/40701084|url-status=dead}} He was waived by the Mavericks on October 22 after appearing in seven preseason games.{{cite web|first=Bobby|last=Karalla|url=http://www.mavs.com/mavericks-request-waivers-five-set-opening-night-roster/|title=Mavericks request waivers on five, set opening night roster|work=Mavs.com|date=October 22, 2016|access-date=October 22, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161023140647/http://www.mavs.com/mavericks-request-waivers-five-set-opening-night-roster/|archive-date=October 23, 2016|url-status=dead}} He later re-signed with the team on November 18{{cite web|first=Bobby|last=Karalla|url=https://www.mavs.com/mavericks-sign-free-agent-guard-jonathan-gibson/|title=Mavericks sign free agent guard Jonathan Gibson|work=Mavs.com|date=November 18, 2016|access-date=November 18, 2016}} and made his NBA debut that night. With the Mavericks missing their top three options at point guard—[[Deron Williams]], [[J. J. Barea]] and [[Devin Harris]]—all due to injury, Gibson backed-up [[Seth Curry]] off the bench and had 11 points and a team-high three assists in an 80–64 loss to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899630|title=Parsons leads Grizzlies over Mavs 80–64 in return to Dallas|work=ESPN.com|date=November 18, 2016|access-date=November 19, 2016}} The following night, he scored a game-high 26 points off the bench in a 95–87 loss to the [[Orlando Magic]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899637|title=Magic use late surge to beat Mavericks 95–87|work=ESPN.com|date=November 19, 2016|access-date=November 20, 2016}} He became the first undrafted player to score 26 points in his first or second game since [[Lloyd Daniels]] in 1992.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899656|title=Leonard scores 24 as Spurs top struggling Mavericks 96–91|work=ESPN.com|date=November 21, 2016|access-date=November 22, 2016}} He appeared in 11 straight games for the Mavericks while averaging 9.2 points in 18.6 minutes per game, before dropping out of the rotation and appearing in six of the next eight with just 4.5 minutes per game and registering four scoreless games.{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/g/gibsojo01/gamelog/2017/|title=Jonathan Gibson 2016–17 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=December 27, 2016}} As a result, on December 27, he was waived by the Mavericks.{{cite web|first=Arya|last=Ahmadi|url=https://www.mavs.com/mavericks-sign-free-agent-guard-pierre-jackson/|title=Mavericks sign free-agent guard Pierre Jackson|work=Mavs.com|date=December 27, 5.2 rebounds, 5.5 assists and 2.2 steals per game. ===2017–18 season=== On September 20, 2017, Gibson signed with the [[Qingdao DoubleStar Eagles]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]], returning to the team for a second stint.{{cite web|url=http://sports.163.com/17/0920/19/CUQ3GI630005877V.html|title=吉布森抵青岛调侃老帅叶鹏:你还是只会那几句英语吗|work=163.com|date=September 20, 2017|access-date=September 28, 2017|language=zh}} In 38 games, he averaged 33.7 points, 6.8 rebounds, 4.7 assists and 1.5 steals per game.
